text:
elliot: Heads up — I kicked off the BMC firmware push to eu-west-1 rack-r4 at ~09:00 UTC and we just saw a management power-rail trip on 3 nodes. remote console sessions dropped and one host came back with Secure Boot toggled OFF. Provisioner began evicting GPUs immediately. @tanya can you pause the rollout?

tanya: Pausing rollout now. Set gate to manual in the deploy system. :warning: Can you paste the node IDs?

elliot: Nodes: r4-n22, r4-n23, r4-n24. Quick logs: 
```
[2026-03-20T09:01:12Z] bmc-watchdog: power-rail-fault detected
[2026-03-20T09:01:13Z] oob: session dropped, resetting management NIC
[2026-03-20T09:01:19Z] firmware-update: reflash succeeded, secureboot=0
```

sachin: :eyes: Provisioner eviction summary from the autoscaler: 42 GPUs evicted across 12 pods in eu-west-1. We're seeing a 32% drop in allocatable GPU capacity, queue length spiking.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-834 created by elliot — "mgmt-rail-trip during BMC fw push causing secureboot flag drift and GPU eviction". Priority P2. Link: https://incidents.redwood/int/INC-2026-834

lee: Quick triage: is this a hardware power rail issue or a side-effect of the BMC rewrite? Any diff in the fw package?

marie: I pulled the firmware artifact: checksum matches the known-good build (sha256: ab12...ef34). No config changes in the package. Hardware telemetry shows a transient undervolt on the 3 affected nodes at exactly 09:01:11. Could be a PSU hiccup coincident with the flash.

oncall-robin: Running oob session checks now: `oobctl sessions --nodes r4-n22,r4-n23,r4-n24 --verbose`

oncall-robin: Output (snip):
```
node r4-n22: console reconnect OK, secure_boot=disabled, last_reboot=2026-03-20T09:01:20Z
node r4-n23: console recon failed, bmc-state=watchdog-reset
node r4-n24: console reconnect OK, secure_boot=disabled
```

elliot: Thanks. For immediate mitigation I recommend: 1) Allow only manual reflash, 2) Re-enable secureboot flag check in the provisioner (temporary fail-open currently), 3) Migrate queued workloads to eu-central-1 until we stabilize. Anyone object?

tanya: +1 on manual only. On (2) — the provisioner check lives in deploy-agent v2.4. We can flip the flag server-side to treat secureboot mismatch as warning until we have hardware confirmation. Will do now.

sachin: I'll kick off migrations for high-priority queues. ETA ~18m to shift warm containers and reduce eviction pressure. Cost note: moving 42 GPUs cross-region will add roughly ~$6k/hr while the migration runs — flagging for finance.

lee: Also recommend adding a pre-flash power sanity check: query BMC telemetry for PSU voltage stable for 30s before flashing. If not stable, skip auto-flash and put node into manual review. Save runbook snippet: 
```
if bmc.read(psu_voltage).stdev > 0.2V:
  mark node MANUAL_REVIEW
  abort flash
```

marie: Agree. Will open a ticket to add the PSU sanity gate into the firmware pipeline. We should also schedule a hardware vendor RMA on r4-n23 after we stabilize it — logs show repeated watchdog resets.

elliot: Current status: rollout paused, provisioner set to warn-on-secboot, migrations started, incident created. Next steps: hardware triage for r4-n23, add pre-flash PSU gate, postmortem scheduled 24h from now.

tanya: Adding follow-up tasks to the incident and assigning owners. I'll also notify sales about potential customer impact in eu-west-1 if we expect degraded capacity >2h.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-834 updated: severity P2 -> P1 (capacity impact estimating >1h). Assigned: marie (HW triage), sachin (migrations), lee (pipeline gate), tanya (incident lead).

sachin: Migration kicked off. Progress: 12% moved, queue depth decreasing. Will update in 10m.

lee: Logged the pipeline gate PR: https://git.redwood/infra/firmware/pulls/782 — includes unit tests and BMC telemetry mock.

marie: RMA requested for r4-n23 with vendor (ticket VND-4492). They want serial logs and power-cycling history — attaching incident logs to the vendor ticket.

oncall-robin: Final note: we need to treat "management rail trip coincident with flash" as a known hazard. Suggest adding it to the pre-deploy checklist and an automated abort on any PSU ADC anomaly.

elliot: Agree. Closing loop here — will post incident update to #incidents and schedule the postmortem. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
